newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner gave execs stock options in '96.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner gave execs stock options in '96.

text.p: Time Warner Inc granted its top executives new stock options instead of pay raises in 1996, a move analysts said is aimed at boosting the company's sluggish stock price.

The New York-based media and entertainment company, whose shares stood around $42 each in midday trading Monday, said in its proxy statement it gave Chairman Gerald Levin 350,000 options while keeping his salary at $1.05 million and his bonus at $4 million, the same he has been paid since 1994.

The company gave Vice Chairman Ted Turner, who joined the company on October 10 after Time Warner acquired Turner Broadcasting, 1.3 million options as well as a salary of about $235,000 and a $1 million bonus for his three months at the company.
Turner, whose annual salary is the same as Levin's, is due another 1.2 million options over the next four years, Time Warner said.

Exactly half of Levin's new options -- called "step-up options" -- can be exercised at $42.63, 25 percent at $53.29 and 25 percent at $63.95, a Time Warner spokesman said. Half of Turner's options can be exercised at $41.25, although the rest cannot be exercised until the stock touches $51.56 or higher. At about $42 per share, Time Warner's stock is trading about where it was this time last year, despite record levels of U.S. stock markets.
Analysts said that stock price is a major issue for the company.
"They're interetsed in getting that stock price moving in the right direction," said Michael Kupinski, an analyst at A.G. Edwards. "They're incentivizing management to get the price moving."
